samples.text:
The plans show Grange Park in 1980 when it was opened and how it looks today. In general, the park have more facilities for sport and leisure now, but the lake and the main paths are the same.

In 1980 there was a lake in the centre of the park, with a main path from the west and a footpath to the east. There was trees in the north-west and south-east, tennis courts in the south-west, flower gardens in the north and a café and toilets in the north-east.

Today, the tennis courts has been replaced by a skate park and the trees in the south-east was changed into an outdoor gym. The flower gardens became a wildflower meadow, and some trees in the north-west were removed to build a children's playground. Also, the café is bigger now and it is a café and visitor centre. The toilets moved to the south, next to the café. Another change is a new cycle path from the south of the park to the lake, and a car park was built in the south next to it.
samples.why: Basic overview · most changes covered though some are listed mechanically · repetitive linking · adequate vocabulary with some imprecision · several agreement and preposition errors that do not affect understanding.

samples.text:
The plans illustrate the layout of Grange Park when it first opened in 1980 and its present-day design. Overall, the park has shifted from a traditional, largely green space towards one offering more active leisure facilities, although its central lake and the main paths leading to it have been retained.

In the southern half of the park, the tennis courts in the south-west have been converted into a skate park, while the trees in the south-east have been cleared to make room for an outdoor gym. In addition, a new cycle path now runs north from the southern edge of the park to the lake, and a car park has been built beside it, to the west.

The northern part has also been transformed. The trees in the north-west have been reduced, and a children's playground now occupies the land next to them. The flower gardens have been replaced by a smaller wildflower meadow, and the café in the north-east has been expanded into a café and visitor centre. Lastly, the toilets, which were located in the north-eastern corner, has been moved a little further south, next to the café.
samples.why: Clear overview identifying a change in character · key changes organised logically by area · range of linking devices · some less common vocabulary · mostly accurate with a minor agreement slip.

samples.text:
The two plans show Grange Park at its opening in 1980 and as it appears today. The most notable development is that much of the park's natural and ornamental landscape has been replaced by facilities for active recreation, while its core layout, the central lake with paths approaching from the west and east, has survived intact.

In 1980, the park was dominated by greenery: woodland occupied both the north-west and the south-east, and a large area of flower gardens lay to the north of the lake. The only facilities were tennis courts in the south-west and a café and toilets in the north-east.

Since then, the tennis courts have been turned into a skate park, and the south-eastern woodland has given way to an outdoor gym. The trees in the north-west have been cut back to make space for a children's playground, and the flower gardens have been replaced by a somewhat smaller wildflower meadow. The café has been enlarged to incorporate a visitor centre, with the toilets relocated from the far corner to a spot just east of it. Access has also been improved, with a cycle path now leading from the southern boundary to the lake and a car park alongside it.
samples.why: Incisive overview capturing the change in the park's character · effective before-and-after organisation · smooth cohesion · precise vocabulary (ornamental, cut back, incorporate) · wide range of accurate complex structures.
